decision: Transparent alternative segmentation is already positively established by1201. Actual fixed substring shorthand is already concretely specified by933/935, including canonical priority and open literal spelling. No new writer card or experiment follows merely by allowing multi-letter expansions. The useful new clarification is the conditional all-singletons expansion theorem and its literal-alphabet cost, stated below.

all_singletons_confluence_theorem.premises: Let A be the physical working-unit alphabet. Every singleton a in A is a legal decoding entry with a fixed expansion e(a) into a source-letter string. Every longer entry c=a1...ak has a fixed expansion e(c). All relevant entry concatenations, including the full singleton segmentation of c, are admissible. Different admissible segmentations of one physical string must return the same source string.
all_singletons_confluence_theorem.conclusion: For every longer entry c, e(c)=e(a1)...e(ak). Consequently every admissible whole physical string w has expansion E(w), where E is the homomorphism determined solely by the singleton expansions.
all_singletons_confluence_theorem.proof: Compare the one-entry parse [c] with the always-admissible singleton parse [a1,...,ak]. Meaning uniqueness forces their expansions to agree. Replacing every longer entry of any parse by its singleton sequence then leaves both the physical string and its expanded source unchanged.
all_singletons_confluence_theorem.what_is_not_new: Adding such a longer physical block to the reader's memory changes how it is recognized, not its printed bytes, length or content. C={a->x,b->y,ab->xy} supplies no new writing effect. This is the same transparent-chunk principle as1201, not another statistical writer.
all_singletons_confluence_theorem.important_qualification: The expansions e(a) need not each contain one source letter. An atomic output sign may expand to a multi-letter substring; that can actually shorten writing. The theorem excludes an independent extra meaning for a longer PHYSICAL chunk, not every singleton shorthand sign.

literal_alphabet_capacity_corollary.premises: Require a general literal route for every finite string over an independently writable source alphabet Sigma of size m, using only the all-singleton homomorphic expansion above. Expansions are fixed and non-erasing; ordinary source-letter spelling, including unfamiliar names, is recovered exactly.
literal_alphabet_capacity_corollary.proof: For each source letter x, the complete one-letter source string x must have some output w. Since every unit expansion is nonempty and their concatenation has length1, w consists of one output unit a with e(a)=x. Different source letters require different such units. Thus at least m output units are already committed to single-letter expansions.
literal_alphabet_capacity_corollary.consequence: With exactly22 output units and m=22 independently writable source letters, every output unit is consumed by the ordinary literal alphabet. There is no spare atomic sign for a genuinely multi-letter expansion. With m<22, at most22-m atomic signs remain for shortcuts. With m>22, that unrestricted literal contract is impossible in this all-singletons form.
literal_alphabet_capacity_corollary.limits: This is conditional on the universal literal route and the freely admissible singleton parse. It does not forbid a restricted source vocabulary or an alphabet with orthographic dependencies, nor a paid escape/control grammar whose marker is not a free literal singleton. Those are different complete contracts. It does not identify any native source alphabet or assert that all22 native working signs are literal codes.

canonicality_is_not_free_confluence.counterexample: If a->x, b->y and ab->z with z different from xy, longest-match decoding can select z, but it cannot also recover the literal input xy if its writer emits the same ab. One message is lost unless a separate written spelling, escape or input restriction is supplied.
canonicality_is_not_free_confluence.scope: Merely saying that all singleton entries exist does not force their concatenation to be an admissible parse under a restricted grammar. The theorem above explicitly assumes it is admissible. A canonical parser that forbids that parse must be paired with a complete source encoder and paid alternative literal spelling; a decoder preference alone is insufficient.
canonicality_is_not_free_confluence.prior: GDT1201 explicitly retains the independent-whole-value collision and notes that longest-match selection cannot recover both inputs. No new meaning card or old573/616 value is used here.

existing_hand_contract_933.rule: Ordinary26-letter literal drawings plus two distinct atomic shorthand drawings MU=AB and NU=BC. Scan each source word once from the left; consume AB or BC whenever matched, otherwise one literal. Expand every output atom literally and re-encode to check canonicality. Spaces stop matches; words repeat unchanged.
existing_hand_contract_933.paid_difference: ABC writes MU followed by literal C under left priority, whereas right priority writes literal A followed by NU. These are genuinely different written outputs for the same source spelling. The shorthand drawings are not the physical two-letter strings they replace.
existing_hand_contract_933.cost: 26 literal drawings plus2 shortcut drawings and one-letter lookahead. This is not already a22-sign physical realization.
existing_hand_contract_933.later_decision: Under free source/key binding and at most25 observed output types, two types can be shortcuts and every other type an unrelated D-Z literal. The ordinary A/B/C drawings remain unobserved, so every output is canonical under both directions at every length. Hence unbound surface coverage, even with active shortcuts, cannot select this writer. That constructive limitation remains; no renewed missing-binding audit is proposed.

existing_paid_22sign_contract_935.rule: The exact16 source substrings have fixed two-unit shortcut codes. At each source position choose the longest listed match; otherwise fully spell one character. Unknown words use the same scan, not a new word table. Preserve whole source-token boundaries. Decode the marked shortcut or literal character packets, then require exact canonical re-encoding.
existing_paid_22sign_contract_935.teaching_example: The invented ordinary instruction 'schneide nicht' becomes the abstract output sequence [shortcut(sch), literal(n), literal(e), literal(i), literal(d), literal(e)] followed by [shortcut(nicht)]. Each abstract packet has its already declared physical spelling in the raw table. Expanding gives the same two source words, including the negative word; this is not a native word assignment or a newly executed example.
existing_paid_22sign_contract_935.paid_controls: The19 ordinary one-unit signs are literal lowercase entries. q introduces one selector for the remaining lowercase letters; y introduces two rare-character selectors; r introduces one of16 substring selectors. Thus q/y/r are not free literal singletons. The carrier avoids the all-singletons premise by explicit parsing rules, not by freely inferring context.
existing_paid_22sign_contract_935.paid_table: The declared lesson contains26 lowercase correspondences,56 listed rare-character correspondences and16 exact substring expansions, with22 physical working units. Code entries and physical alphabet size are different costs. The98 expansion entries are not98 independent source letters:16 are multi-letter strings. This known larger lesson is not an automatic26/28 expansion of the1235 model.
existing_paid_22sign_contract_935.scope_cost: Names are retained only over the declared finite character inventory; unlisted characters are rejected. Rare characters can be expensive. Whole words are moved intact across physical lines; a truly overwide word has no free continuation escape. The lesson assumes normal source-language competence and does not teach a technical meaning merely by spelling its name.
existing_paid_22sign_contract_935.careful_execution_status: 1179A actually used the935 longest-match spelling, plus its separately fixed short-word pairing and paid inner boundary. Its complete source inverse passed, its full statistical screen failed. That is an executed descendant, not proof that every935 grouping variant was run; it also prevents presenting this already implemented shorthand component as a newly untried discovery.

word_frequency_debt.fact: A fixed deterministic encoder per source word with an exact inverse is injective per word: two distinct source words cannot emit the same output word. Therefore complete-word type identities and frequencies remain unchanged even when individual substrings shorten the spelling.
word_frequency_debt.retained_scope: The old four-source one-token/one-group capacity exclusion applies when those same source projections and boundary assumptions are adopted. It is not a general rejection of shorthand, another language, changed grouping or declared semantic content. Changing those assumptions requires its own complete contract; no such repair is selected here.
word_frequency_debt.consequence: Transparent chunk recognition alone changes no written statistic. Actual fixed shortening can change lengths and glyph transitions but does not by itself solve incompatible whole-word frequency partitions.

access_and_stop: Route/topic, bounded ideas show/duplicates,1201 followups, route-check and listed primary texts only. No raw native/source data, image, new corpus, encoder, count, fitting, GDT or root-file mutation. Mathematical toy strings and the invented instruction were checked by hand only. No new RAW card is warranted for a duplicate mechanism; block stops with this clarification.
